title: Indus & rongorongo
question: When do similar signs become evidence of a connection?
finding: Under this catalogue metric, the pair ranked near the middle of the comparison set. Rankings changed when font controls were distorted to resemble scanned drawings; the famous chart also differs from the catalogue forms.
limitations: The combined metric retrieved the correct independent rendition first in about 75% of validation queries, below HOG alone at about 81%. Its results describe this representation and metric; they do not settle perceived resemblance, linguistic affinity or historical contact.

title: Birds, serpents & sacred centres
question: Do the familiar motifs travel together?
finding: In the sampled catalogue, the three broad motif classes are widespread. Their bundle does not stand out against the study's documentation-preserving comparisons.
limitations: Broad keyword classes are not a test of this bird-and-disc composition. Coverage is uneven, and missing catalogue entries are not evidence of absence. Geographic dispersion alone cannot distinguish invention from transmission.

title: The pillar & the moai
question: Can AI measure the resemblance people see?
finding: The saved responses expose perception errors as well as prompt and presentation effects. Opus placed the pair near the top of its distant comparisons; GPT-5.5 ranked many more alternatives above it. Those disagreeing observations remain available.
limitations: Some judges described a face on the moai’s back or missed its bird figures. The prompts also mixed visible similarity with shared-origin judgments. These pilots cannot establish that the resemblance is ordinary, exceptional or historically explained.

title: The civilisers
question: Where does the resemblance between teaching figures come from?
finding: V1's claimed partners ranked first in 62.5% of completed lineups, versus 9% for random pairs. The new V2 audit inspects 29 source passages; it has not rerun the similarity test.
limitations: The lineups were recognisable and used compressed modern accounts. The new audit is small, purposively selected and unblinded; neither establishes a worldwide rarity rate or a shared origin.

title: The raven & the dove
question: What is shared, and what is regional, in flood stories?
finding: The coded summaries show regional clustering and an uneven distribution of details associated with Genesis, alongside widespread generic flood motifs.
limitations: Regional structure is compatible with ancient inheritance. Recording after contact does not establish borrowing. One AI coded a compiler's summaries, not a representative collection of original accounts.
